To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nitric oxide (NO)/cGMP pathway is involved in the control of male sexual behavior, specifically in the activation of ejaculation‐related neurons in the preoptic and amygdaloid nuclei.
nitric oxide is produced by a large number of ejaculation‐related neurons, that many of these neurons also contain androgen receptor, and that many of them are sensitive to testosterone.

nitric oxide synthase (Nos1) is expressed by many neurons in the medial preoptic and posterodorsal amygdaloid nuclei of male gerbils that express Fos at ejaculation, and that these cells contain the androgen receptor and are sensitive to testosterone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of male sexual behavior.
how the male brain regulates the male reproductive system and how it responds to the female during mating.
understanding how testosterone affects sexual behaviors in male mammals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NO system is an integral part of the neural network that regulates male reproductive behavior.
NO‐containing cells in the posterodrosal preoptic nucleus and the medial part of medial preoptic nucleus are activated at ejaculation, and they may be regulated by testosterone.
the NO‐producing neurons in the PdPN and the lateral MeApd are activated at ejaculation and that they are androgen‐sensitive and testosterone‐regulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NO system is a potential synchronizer of ejaculation‐related neurons, and it may be regulated by testosterone in a manner that differs from that of the classic AR pathway.
nitric oxidergicity is a common characteristic of ejaculation‐related cells in the gerbil forebrain and that testosterone is involved in their nitric oxidergeticity.
NO is involved in mating behavior, and it is a potential mediator for synchronization of ejaculation‐related neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nitric oxide (NO), a gas that is produced by neurons and diffuses to other neurons, is involved in ejaculation in male rats.
nitric oxide may be involved in the synchrony of the ejaculation-related neurons in the forebrain of male gerbils, and the nitric oxide system is under the control of the male hormone, testosterone.
NO is involved in the regulation of sexual behavior in gerbils and that NO is a good candidate to mediate the synchrony in neuronal activity between the PdPN and MeApd at ejaculation.
